name: Nawathinehena
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Arapahoan variety known only from old vocabulary; Goddard 2001 pp.74-76 is classificatory, not a phonology

sources.citation: Wikipedia contributors. 'Nawathinehena language'. Wikipedia (raw wikitext downloaded 2026-09-17).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; only segmental history (*r,*θ,*s > t; *w > m) citing Goddard 1974 and Jacques 2013; states the language is documented only in Kroeber's 1899 vocabulary.

sources.citation: Kroeber, A. L. 1916. Arapaho dialects. University of California Publications in American Archaeology and Ethnology 12(3): 71-138. Berkeley: University of California Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Nawathinehena. The dialect is treated on pp. 73-74 (informant situation, 1899), pp. 75-76 (comparative vocabulary column 'Southern People, Naⁿwaθinähänaⁿ', ~64 items from Tall Bear) and pp. 81-82 (segmental correspondences only: m retained, n>t, s/h/x reflexes, parasitic x before t). The sole accent remark in the paper (p. 83, 'Final vowels, unless long or accented, are surd or whispered') sits in Part II 'Sketch of Arapaho Proper' and applies to Arapaho proper, not to this dialect. A few acute marks appear on some vocabulary forms but are nowhere explained for Nawathinehena.
